maria: Heads-up — scorecard deltas look inverted for the fp8 vs int8 comparison on the new runner. Top-line shows int8 winning by ~3% but the drilldown samples show int8 failures. Anyone else seeing this?

akshay: Yep, saw that this morning in /evals/scorecards. Strange: aggregate +3% for int8 but lots of sample-level regressions. Might be an ingestion/aggregation issue. @jen any idea?

jen: Can you paste the scorecard link and a couple sample ids? I can try to repro locally if I can pull runner artifacts.

maria: https://console.redwood.eval/scorecards/abc123 — sample ids: s_408, s_409, s_410. Quick paste from the diffpanel drilldown output: 
```
# diffpanel CSV parse output (snippet)
samples,metric:int8,metric:fp8
s_408,0.92,0.85
s_409,0.00,0.78
s_410,0.95,0.94
```

sam: FYI CI failed to publish runner#2345 artifacts earlier due to an uploader timeout. I kicked the job and re-ran the uploader for 2346.

ci-bot: runner-ci: job 2346 completed, status=SUCCESS, logs: https://ci.redwood/2346/logs

maria: Interesting — the CSV header uses a colon in metric names, e.g. `metric:int8`. I think our CSV loader normalizes headers by splitting on `:` which may collapse columns into a single metric key. That would explain the flipped aggregate.

akshay: Agreed. Parser is doing a naive split. Quick patch suggestion: sanitize headers by replacing `:` with `__` before parsing so they stay distinct. Example: 
```python
# eval-ingest/parser.py (quickfix)
header = header_line.strip()
sanitized = re.sub(r':', '__', header)
cols = sanitized.split(',')
```

jen: On it — I'll push a small patch to ingest and trigger a reindex for runner#2346 once artifact is confirmed. If artifacts are missing we'll need to re-run the eval job.

artifact-uploader: upload completed: runner#2346 -> s3://redwood-eval/artifacts/2346.tar.gz

sam: Confirmed artifact exists for 2346. Kicking reindex now.

jen: Reindex job started (job id reindex-879). Will post status.

maria: Thanks all — I'll watch the scorecard after reindex. If numbers still look off I'll open a short postmortem. :rocket:

akshay: small follow-up: we should add a unit test in eval-ingest for header chars (colon, slash, spaces) to prevent regressions.

jen: Agreed. Adding test and a changelog note.

maria: awesome, closing loop when reindex finishes. :+1:
